name: UNICEF USA
mission: Over eight decades, the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) has built an unprecedented global support system for the world's children. UNICEF relentlessly works day in and day out to deliver the essentials that give every child an equitable chance in life: health care and immunizations, safe water and sanitation, nutrition, education, emergency relief and more. UNICEF USA advances the global mission of UNICEF by rallying the American public to support the world's most vulnerable children. Together, we have helped save more children's lives than any other humanitarian organization.
theoryOfChange: UNICEF, which includes UNICEF USA's work, utilizes a results-based model where the assumptions or hypotheses about inputs, activities, outputs, and outcomes necessary to achieve desired results for children are considered their theories of change. This framework details a four-level structure: Country Programme, Outcomes, Outputs, and Activities, used for planning, tracking, and demonstrating results. Additionally, UNICEF USA's Impact Fund for Children has co-developed a 'Child-Lens Investment Framework' that guides investors in advancing positive child outcomes and minimizing harm. The UNICEF USA Child Friendly Cities Initiative also employs a 'Framework for Action' that outlines goals, results, and strategies for building child-friendly communities.

Its institutional fundraising engine is efficient, spending only <cite id="1">$0.10 per $1 raised</cite> in contributions. rich_narrative.summary: UNICEF USA supports global child health and development, operating as a major US fundraising arm for global child survival programs. In FY2025 filings based on 2023 financial reporting, the organization reported <cite id="3">$829,050,932 in total revenue</cite>. While holding a <cite id="1">97/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, the organization's audited filed numbers show a <cite id="3">78.3% program expense ratio</cite>, though its cash-adjusted program ratio evaluates to 78% for scoring benchmarks. The charity's overall performance reflects a balanced mix of massive international reach and administrative overhead typical of large fundraising intermediaries. Recent financial filings indicate that revenue declined by 13% moving into FY2024, coming in at $720,404,955. On direct delivery, UNICEF USA provides clear outcome evidence, including <cite id="9">treating children for severe acute malnutrition</cite> and delivering emergency humanitarian relief globally.
